subject: Discovery: SDK + Rerank Integration Playbook
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@bluemesa.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery: SDK + Rerank Integration Playbook

Alex — thanks for taking time today. Quick written recap so we have alignment and clear next steps. I pulled together the integration playbook items we discussed and attached a short requirements doc and a draft SOW for your legal team to review.

Key pain points you reiterated
- Latency spikes on your current embedding/rerank pipeline during peak hourly traffic (~5x baseline).
- Inconsistent relevance for short-query reranking (title-only searches) that hurts CTR.
- Need for predictable per-query cost given large nightly batch reranks.

Outcome you want
- Sub-200ms tail latency for single-query rerank in the 95th percentile for your interactive UI.
- A hybrid approach: streaming generation for live assistant flows + batched embedding/rerank for nightly jobs.
- A repeatable SDK integration path so your product team can ship in two sprints.

Product fit + recommended path (what we discussed)
1) Sandbox + SDK: Ship our lightweight SDK (Node + Python) into a UAT build. Start with our streaming response path for the assistant flows to measure p95. We’ll provide a sandbox key scoped to non-prod.
2) Rerank strategy: Use our embeddings API for nightly index refresh, then call a 2-stage reranker in inference: (a) fast embedding cosine top-k, (b) short-list rerank with a small instruction-tuned model. This reduces compute by ~6x vs brute-force transformer rerank.
3) Function calling + structured output: For the assistant, we recommend structured outputs (JSON schema) to normalize downstream actions. We’ll help you map one function (create_ticket) as a concrete starter to validate the approach.
4) Streaming knobs: Conservative chunk size with prefix caching for the assistant flows. We’ll propose a default batch/window config that balances latency and throughput.
5) Cost controls: Start with our per-route quotas and automated fallback to quantized model variants during spikes.

Open technical questions we agreed to answer
- Your expected average and peak tokens per rerank request (you said ~40 tokens average, confirm peak).
- Whether your embedding index lives in-house or you’ll host it in our managed vector store.
- Data residency needs for logs and KV cache snapshot retention.

Next steps (owners & timeline)
- Redwood: provide sandbox credentials and a sample SDK integration repo + a 2-week pilot runbook (owner: Vivek). ETA: Tue, 2026-07-13.
- BlueMesa: confirm expected qps, peak token size, and whether you’ll use managed vectors or host (owner: Alex). ETA: Mon, 2026-07-12.
- Legal: review attached SOW draft and flag any data/residency language (owner: BlueMesa legal). ETA: Fri, 2026-07-16.

Attachments: BM-Enterprise-Integration-Requirements.pdf (requirements + API examples), SOW-draft-BM-v1.docx (initial commercial terms).

If that looks right I’ll open the sandbox and ping you with keys + a short demo repo. Happy to hop on a follow-up call next week to walk the eng leads through the SDK flow.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery: SDK + Rerank Integration Playbook

Thanks Tessa — good summary. A few quick clarifications from our side after the call: 

1) Tokens and QPS
- Average tokens per candidate for rerank: ~35 tokens. Peak concurrent UI QPS during marketing pushes: ~220 qps. Nightly batch rerank window: ~1.2M queries running over 3 hours.

2) Embedding index
- We prefer to keep the embedding index in our AWS account (for existing snapshot tooling), but are open to using your managed vector store if there are clear SLA and encryption guarantees. Can you provide a short doc comparing managed vs self-hosted vector options?

3) Function calling / structured outputs
- We liked the JSON schema idea. For MVP we want two functions: create_ticket and fetch_customer_profile. Can you confirm how you version schemas and how schema validation failures are surfaced in streaming flows?

4) Legal / SOW
- Looping in legal to review the SOW. They’ll focus on data retention and audit log export frequency.

5) Timeline
- We can commit eng time next week for SDK trial (2 engineer-days). If your sandbox + repo are available by Tue 7/13 we’ll slot it in.

Appreciate the proposed pilot runbook. Also: would you be able to provide an estimate of expected cost delta vs our current brute-force rerank for both the interactive and nightly batch scenarios (ballpark is fine)? That will help get procurement buy-in.

—Alex
Alex Nguyen
Head of Product Engineering
BlueMesa Analytics
